containment.rationale: Nothing experimental to contain; what little framework coupling exists is already confined to loaders, entry points and one vite config, all of which would be trivial to swap.

findings.issue: Minified build artifacts (server/ and dist/) are committed to the repo and npm start runs them; they inflate the review surface, made the static analyzer count framework internals as app code, and can drift from a rebuild.
findings.suggestion: Add app/server and app/dist to .gitignore and rely on npm run build before npm start; the build already regenerates identical output.

findings.issue: undici is declared as a devDependency (^7.0.0) but is statically imported by the production server bundle (server/entry.node-server.js imports {fetch,Headers,Request,Response,FormData} from 'undici'); it only resolves because @builder.io/qwik-city itself depends on undici.
findings.suggestion: Move undici to dependencies, or drop the explicit pin and rely on qwik-city's transitive dependency, so an --omit=dev production install cannot break the server at import time.

summary: The app is deliberately conservative: it uses only long-stable Qwik City v1 APIs, at the current stable version (1.20.3, released 2026-10-25), with no experimental, preview or unstable features anywhere in source. The lone 'experimental' marker is Qwik core's serializer warning string in committed build output, not an API the app calls. The only nits are repository hygiene — committed build artifacts and a mis-tiered undici dependency — neither of which affects runtime stability.
